project_tracker_diagnostic: Perennial/subshrub with winged petiole bases that often fuse into conspicuous nodal discs; yellow-orange heads usually solitary or in 2s–3s; rough foliage.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Common, conspicuous, or high-value comparison species for Central Texas field ID.

morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite; petiole bases dilated/winged and often fused across the node into a disc; blades ovate, sometimes 3-lobed.
morphology_keys.heads: Usually solitary, sometimes 2–3; rays light orange-yellow, often brown/purple-lined beneath.
morphology_keys.fruit: Cypselae often with pappus absent or minute.
best_field_traits: At an intact stem node, inspect the conspicuously widened petiole bases that may connect into a winged or disc-like bridge across the stem; photograph both sides of the node.
Opposite ovate to sometimes three-lobed leaves; shape alone is variable.
Yellow-orange sunflower-like heads; inspect underside bracts and mature cypselae to confirm the genus/species.
Compare other opposite-leaved yellow-headed Asteraceae: verify the fused or expanded petiole-base architecture rather than identifying from yellow rays alone.
Check whether an image actually resolves the nodal disc before placing an arrow.

photo_strategy.selection_logic: Prefer curated taxon photos plus multiple views from one Central Texas/Texas observation.
photo_strategy.remaining_need: NEEDS_DIAGNOSTIC_PHOTO: sharp front/side macro of fused petiole bases at an intact node, involucre and fruit. annotation_pending for any node arrow until image pixels and adaptation permission verified.
